notes.1a: Most candidates recognised that arthropods have a number of pairs of jointed legs.
notes.1bi: Most gave the correct response to this question.
notes.1bii: Candidates correctly identified the organism and some candidates were able to give a feature that is specific to crustaceans.
notes.1ci: and (ii) The organism was correctly identified by nearly all candidates and most were also able to give the correct group name.
notes.2a: and (b) There was an excellent understanding shown of the organisation within the organ in these two questions. The commonest error was to put organ system and organ in the wrong order.
notes.3ai: Most candidates gave a correct response.
notes.3aii: Although candidates understood its position in the food chain, many were unclear about the role of the producer.
notes.3aiii: and (iv) Most candidates answered both questions correctly.
notes.3av: This question was generally answered in term of who eats whom, rather than energy transfer.
notes.3b: There were many excellent answers demonstrating a good understanding of the relationships in a food chain.
notes.4ai: Most candidates gave the correct response.
notes.4aii: There were some very good answers, but some responses gave the cause of no habitat rather than the effect of its destruction.
notes.4b: This question was generally well answered. A common error was to give reasons for disruption of the food web rather than destruction of the habitat itself.
notes.4c: Most candidates were able to describe at least one method of conservation, while many gave a number of methods.
notes.4d: This proved to be a challenging question for some. The best responses ensured that the answers in each cell matched the heading and the other columns.
notes.5a: This question was well answered by the majority of candidates.
notes.5b: Most responses did not recognise that breeds of horses all belong to the same species (this information was in the question stem), so did not recall the word for differences within species.
notes.5c: There were very good attempts to describe the process of selective breeding, with many candidates correctly suggesting the selection of traits. Fewer went on to suggest selecting offspring or repeating over many generations.
notes.5d: While some responses successfully compared natural selection with selective breeding, most were not comparative and just described animals ‘selecting their own partners’ or the process of artificial insemination.
notes.6ai: and (ii) Many candidates gave the correct responses to these questions.
notes.6bi: Although most candidates could define the function of an enzyme, few identified it as a protein.
notes.6biii: and (iv) Many candidates read the correct values from the graph, to work out the increase in reaction rate and then the optimum temperature. One error was to read the y- axis instead of the x-axis .
notes.6c: Most candidates gave the correct response.
notes.6d: Many responses gave a good explanation of the use of pectinase.
notes.6e: There were many excellent answers to this question, showing that candidates had a good understanding of food hygiene.
notes.7ai: Excellent responses were seen for this question.
notes.7aii: Most candidates answered correctly. A common error was to give the name of the blood cell instead of what the cell does.
notes.7bii: While most candidates understood that antibiotics do not work against HIV, fewer could clearly explain why.
notes.7biii: There were many excellent responses on controlling the spread of STIs. One misconception was that the contraceptive pill would protect against STIs.
notes.8ai: This question was generally well answered, with most candidates getting the letter of the part correct, but not always matching the name. A common misconception was that urea is produced in the kidney.
notes.8aii: Many were unclear as to whether egestion occurs in the anus or the rectum.
notes.8aiii: A few responses indicated that hydrochloric acid kills bacteria. The commonest error was that it digests food.
notes.8b: This question was well answered by many candidates. The commonest errors were using the words ureter, uterus for urethra and vice versa.
